transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Lena (HorizonWare - Head of ML), Tomás (HorizonWare - Dir Eng), Maya (HorizonWare - PM)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
- Purpose: scope a 6-week POC to evaluate open models for multilingual localization & extraction for HorizonWare's support tooling.
- Key constraints: Spanish/Portuguese support, latency targets, strong entity extraction (PII redaction), privacy (VPC/on-prem preference), target cost.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to share benchmark harness and model shortlist; HorizonWare to provide dataset samples; schedule private capacity check.

Topics:
- Success criteria (accuracy metrics, hallucination tolerances, latency/cost targets)
- Workload sizing (peak qps, average token length, concurrency)
- Benchmark plan (automatic + human evals)
- Timeline & resourcing for POC (6-week proposal)
- Early model shortlist and tradeoffs (large-chat vs smaller quantized)
- Security / deployment options (VPC, KMS, SOC2)

Action items (also listed above): see for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, I'm Aisha from Redwood. quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Lena: yep, good here. thanks.
[00:07] Tomás: all good.
[00:12] Aisha: Awesome. high level—HorizonWare wants a POC to validate a small set of open models for localized support summarization and entity extraction across Spanish, Portuguese, French and English. correct?
[00:21] Maya: correct. and I want to make sure we capture timing - we need results before a product board in mid-june.
[00:28] Marcus: ok so that gives us, what, six weeks-ish. we usually do a two week bench then integration? depends.
[00:36] Lena: exactly. Our main success criteria are extraction precision for PII redaction and overall summary accuracy — we need very low leakage of personal data.
[00:46] Tomás: also latency: our UX needs sub-400ms for 256-token responses in the fast path, and cost per token needs to stay under our projected $0.001 which is tight.
[00:56] Aisha: cool, useful numbers. i'll repeat them to make sure we have them: latency target 400 ms for median p95? do you mean p50 or p95?
[01:04] Tomás: p95 is what we care about. p95 < 400 ms on hosted or dedicated.
[01:10] Marcus: note — p95 on public hosted variants will vary; on dedicated gpus we can get closer. also caching/prefix KV — uh K V cash — can help with repeated prompts.
[01:21] Lena: yeah we have lots of repeatable greetings and templates. caching could cut costs.
[01:26] Maya: timeline constraint: mid-June product board. if bench finishes in two weeks, we need integration + small user trial over the next month. so 6 weeks total.
[01:35] Aisha: Got it. let's talk model shortlist — Marcus, do you want to run through candidates?
[01:39] Marcus: sure. based on their language mix and budget, we propose a mix: a larger chat model for quality baseline, plus cheaper quantized mid-size models for throughput. shortlist idea: Llama2-chat-70B (quantized variants), Mistral-Instruct-13B, MPT-30B-Chat (guest name), Falcon-40B-instruct, and a small multilingual Polyglot-8B.
[02:02] Lena: quick note — vendor names are fine but we need models that were trained on multi-lingual corpora, Spanish/pt especially. Mistral and Polyglot look promising.
[02:10] Tomás: any concerns about hallucinations on instruction models? we can't have creative fabrications when extracting PII.
[02:16] Marcus: yeah that's a core tradeoff. larger models (70B) tend to be better at instruction following and lower hallucination, but cost and latency go up. smaller models need to be tuned and may require stronger guardrails - reranking, grounding, retrieval.
[02:29] Maya: can we do hybrid? route risky requests to larger model fallback?
[02:33] Aisha: absolutely — smart routing is a capability. we can set policy to route by confidence score. if model unsure, escalate to the 70B variant.
[02:40] [02:40] Lena: does Redwood support private VPC or on-prem? we have data residency concerns for a subset of EU customers.
[02:45] Aisha: yes — Redwood Private with VPC and customer-managed KMS is available. we should test whether the customer's infra can host the runtime, and if not, dedicated capacity in a compliant region.
[02:57] Tomás: and SOC2/ISO compliance — we need docs.
[03:00] Aisha: I'll send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and a checklist.
[03:03] Marcus: ok back to benchmarks — we propose the following evaluation plan: automated metrics (chrF/BLEU for translation-ish summarization), extraction F1 for entity/PII extraction, hallucination rate via targeted probes, and human eval for summary usefulness. plus latency and cost measurements under synthetic load.
[03:19] Lena: sounds good. for extraction we have labeled data for 8k examples; we'll push another 2k quick labels.
[03:25] Marcus: perfect. how many concurrent users and average token length? we need that to size throughput.
[03:29] Tomás: peak concurrent 40 req/s, average 180 tokens per request, 95th token length 420.
[03:36] Marcus: noted. that shapes batching and GPU selection. with 40 qps and 180 tokens, continuous batching is important to keep cost low.
[03:45] Maya: can you estimate cost ballpark for each model? at least relative (cheap/moderate/expensive).
[03:50] Marcus: very rough: Polyglot-8B: cheap, Mistral-13B: moderate, MPT/Falcon-30/40B: moderate-high, Llama2-70B: expensive unless aggressively quantized. but we can run quantized variants that cut memory and cost at some small quality cost.
[04:04] Lena: important: we want to measure redaction accuracy — basically false negatives unacceptable. do you have recommended thresholds?
[04:10] Marcus: recommend extraction recall > 0.98 for PII detection and precision > 0.95. if models don't meet recall, add a deterministic regex+NER ensemble to guarantee coverage.
[04:20] Tomás: ok. can Redwood run the regex ensemble as a pre-filter?
[04:24] Marcus: yes, we can add a preprocessor that strips or tags PII before sending to model. that can also be done client-side.
[04:30] [04:30] Maya: about the bench harness, do you need our credentials or will Redwood spin up synthetic traffic?
[04:35] Aisha: both. we'll run internal benchmarks with synthetic traffic mirroring your token lengths, but we need your real examples (anonymized) to measure accuracy.
[04:44] Lena: we'll scrub and anonymize according to the checklist and upload a sample to S3.
[04:48] Marcus: perfect. one more thing — evaluation signals: we will capture model confidence, per-token latency, and tokenization inefficiencies (subword counts) — multilingual tokenization matters a lot for languages with accents.
[05:00] Tomás: good point; Spanish/pt often tokenize more compactly, but portuguese decodes weird sometimes.
[05:06] Aisha: security — we will provide the Private deployment questionnaire. Tomás, you mentioned SSO/SAML?
[05:12] Tomás: yes, we need SSO with SCIM provisioning and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. encryption at rest with customer KMS mandatory.
[05:20] Aisha: noted. Redwood supports KMS/HSM integration and log forwarding. Marcus will scope any additional custom work.
[05:27] Marcus: on the topic of deployment, we should also decide early whether to test on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. tradeoffs: Hosted fast to get started, but not ideal for data residency. Dedicated almost always hits latency SLOs with predictable cost, Private needed for EU PII regs.
[05:45] Lena: we are leaning Private for EU customers and Dedicated for US rollout. initial bench can run in hosted or dedicated — whichever is faster to set up.
[05:55] Maya: question — how do we compare hallucination across models automatically?
[05:58] Marcus: we include targeted probes and we measure divergence against ground truth; low-scoring responses get sent to human raters. we also use factuality checks using retrieval-to-ground and synthetic adversarial cases.
[06:12] Lena: ok. any competitors we should worry about? we've talked to Anthropic about a managed offering and OpenAI for translation. cost was a blocker there.
[06:20] Aisha: understood. we'll try to show cost/latency tradeoffs so your board can weigh options.
[06:26] [06:26] Tomás: agreed. let's walk through the week-by-week proposed plan.
[06:29] Marcus: week 0-1: share dataset and finalize metrics. week 1-2: run bench across 4 candidate models (Llama2-70B quantized, Mistral-13B, Falcon/MPT mid-size, Polyglot-8B). produce initial accuracy+latency report. week 3-4: integration into a small staging flow (edge cases + routing tests). week 5-6: user trial + final report for product board.
[06:52] Maya: that aligns with our mid-June board.
[06:55] Lena: are you able to do human evals in week 2 concurrently? we need a quick sample.
[06:59] Marcus: yes — we can set up a small human evaluation panel for a few hundred examples; it'll take a few days.
[07:06] Aisha: i'll also include pricing scenarios for dedicated vs hosted vs private based on your throughput numbers.
[07:12] Tomás: one blocker — network egress costs for Private on our cloud. any guidance?
[07:18] Marcus: egress depends on your cloud; for on-prem it's minimal. if using dedicated in a cloud region, we can measure egress and include it in cost modeling. we can also recommend local region placement to minimize cost.
[07:29] [07:29] Maya: question on model updates — if we pin a model version and later want to update, can Redwood handle canaries or A/B?
[07:35] Aisha: yes, rollouts and canary policies are supported. we'll canary to a small percentage and monitor regressions via your evaluation suite.
[07:43] Lena: any other integration needs? webhooks?
[07:46] Marcus: yes, Redwood can forward verdicts and metadata via webhooks or we can use a pull API for results.
[07:53] Tomás: ok, last question — will you provide estimated infra sizing (GPU memory) for each model variant?
[07:58] Marcus: yes — we'll include rough GPU types and memory footprint per model in the bench doc. quantized footprints vary.
[08:06] Aisha: great. recap of concrete next steps: Marcus will draft bench scripts and share repo; Aisha sends SOC2 + pricing + private checklist; HorizonWare shares dataset sample and security contact.
[08:18] Lena: we'll aim to get that dataset in by next monday.
[08:21] Tomás: we'll confirm security person and calendar invites for the private-deploy feasibility call.
[08:26] Maya: thanks everyone.
[08:28] Aisha: thank you. we'll follow up in email with timelines and the bench plan.
